edges.description: Ongoing hepatocellular membrane injury releases AST and ALT into the circulation.
Sustained hepatocyte injury and Kupffer-cell signaling activate hepatic stellate cells to deposit fibrotic extracellular matrix.
Progressive fibrotic remodeling of the hepatic parenchyma advances to bridging fibrosis and cirrhosis.
Advanced hepatic fibrosis and cirrhosis elevate portal venous pressure, producing esophageal varices.
Cirrhosis-associated portal hypertension and hypersplenism reduce circulating platelet counts.
Reduced lysosomal free-sterol release triggers compensatory hepatic sterol synthesis and alters lipoprotein secretion, clearance, and vascular foam-cell lipid handling.
